title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: Rolling a Position Under Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
A member on Grain Marketing Contracts who cannot deliver inside the window, or who wants the referenced futures month moved, rolls the position rather than defaulting on it.

**1. The instruction.** A signed roll instruction naming the bushels and the month to be moved to is registered with the grain desk before the roll is executed. Whether it is signed, what kind of instruction it is and what standing it carries are read off the instruction record against the instruction reference; a member's word that they meant to sign it is not that record.

**2. What a programme allows.** A roll may only be taken on programmes whose catalogue allows rolls at all, and the contract may take no more rolls in a crop year than the programme allows; a member at that ceiling is not rolled again and must deliver, buy out or default.

**3. The crop year the ceiling is counted over.** The crop year runs 1 September through 31 August and is named for the calendar year in which it ends, and the rolls counted against the ceiling are the roll confirmations recorded against the contract inside that crop year.

**4. The spread.** The market spread between the two futures months is carried in full to the member, gaining where the market carries and losing where it is inverted.

**5. How it is collected.** Both the spread and the charge are drawn onto the settlement statement of the bushels they attach to rather than invoiced separately.

**6. What a roll does not change.** Rolling moves the delivery window out by the length of the standard window for the programme and does not itself change the bushels committed, so a member who also wants fewer bushels needs an amendment as well.

## Points of judgement on the crop-year count

A roll confirmation recorded on 20 August falls in the crop year ending that 31 August; one recorded on 2 September falls in the next crop year, which is named for the calendar year it ends in. A contract that took two rolls in the crop year ending 31 August 2025 and one since 1 September 2025 stands at one roll against the current year's ceiling.

## Clauses no longer in force

Two clauses of this rule are **no longer in force** and are carried here only so that no reader applies them. The first is the requirement, within clause 2 above, that a roll instruction

> "must name at least the programme's roll minimum"

and the second is the charging sentence

> "The member carries the market spread between the two futures months in full, gaining where the market carries and losing where it is inverted, and pays the programme's administrative charge per bushel rolled on top of it."

The remaining clauses, including the carriage of the spread in full stated at clause 4 and the ceiling on rolls in a crop year, stand as written.
